meta.title: Crewreview: a crew of AI agents for your pull requests
meta.description: Open source. Reviews pull requests with parallel AI lenses and a verifier, and answers the reviews on yours: fixes, replies, resolves. Runs locally with Claude Code, Codex, Kiro or any ACP agent.
nav.label: Main
hero.title_html: Your pull requests, reviewed and answered by a crew of AI agents
hero.lead: Crewreview runs on your machine with the coding agents you already pay for. It reviews other people's pull requests, and answers the reviews on yours: fixes, replies, resolves, asks for another look.
board.label: A review in progress: two lenses reading code, tests and the verifier done, a verdict and an automated reply
board.verdictWhy: decided by a rule, not by a model
board.reply: Clamped the percentage to [0, 1] in src/cart/discount.ts and added a test for 120%.
jobs.title: Two jobs, one crew
jobs.sub: The reviewer looks at your teammates' changes. The attendant takes care of the reviews on yours. Turn each on per repository: off, inbox (waits for your approval) or auto.
jobs.reviewerLead: Several read-only lenses in parallel, a verifier that tries to prove them wrong, and a fixed rule for the verdict.
jobs.r1: Correctness, security, architecture, tests and UI lenses; add your own in the repository.
jobs.r2: Every finding points at a real file and line, or it's dropped.
jobs.r3: Reads the description, the discussion, CI and what changed since its last review; never repeats a point already made.
jobs.r4: Posts one review with inline comments, from your account.
jobs.attendantLead: On your pull requests, it answers each comment: fixed, replied, declined, or left to you.
jobs.a1: Works in its own worktree, never in your clone.
jobs.a2: Runs your checks before pushing; commits with your identity and signature, never force-pushes.
jobs.a3: Replies, resolves fixed threads and asks reviewers to look again.
jobs.a4: The polish loop: review, fix, review again, before you ask a person.
how.title: How a review works
how.sub: The model proposes; code decides. Each step can be checked in the report.
how.s1d: The diff, the description, the discussion, CI and the project's own rules from the base branch.
how.s2d: Read-only agents look at the change in parallel, each through one lens.
how.s3d: Findings without a real file and line are dropped; duplicates are merged.
how.s4d: Another agent, even another vendor, tries to prove each finding wrong.
how.s5d: A fixed rule decides: request changes, comment or approve.
safety.title: Safe by design
safety.sub: Pull request text is written by others, and agents can be talked into things. Crewreview assumes both.
safety.f1d: Reviewers can't write or run commands; a canary test proves it on your machine, per harness version.
safety.f2d: Your git host token stays with Crewreview. Agents get a filtered environment; Crewreview posts and pushes.
safety.f3d: Only people who can push to the repository steer the attendant. Everyone else is ignored.
safety.f4d: Changes to CI, secrets, deployment or the crew's own rules always wait for your approval.
safety.f5: Nothing leaves but to your harness
safety.f5d: No server, no account, no telemetry. Code goes only where the harness you picked sends it.
safety.f6d: Updates install only with a valid signature from the release key built into your binary.
harness.title: Bring the agent you already use
harness.sub: No API key needed: Crewreview drives the coding agents you're signed in to. A second vendor can check the first.
harness.custom: Or describe any CLI in your config. Flags that switch off a harness's safety are refused by a test on every command line Crewreview builds.
crew.title: Watch the crew work
crew.sub: A dashboard on your machine, in five languages, light or dark.
crew.nowd: Every agent at work, live: its lens, its harness, the file it's reading.
crew.inboxd: Reviews and answers waiting for your approval, with findings, replies and diffs.
crew.reposd: Switch each automation off, inbox or auto; see verified harnesses and today's usage.
start.title: Get started
faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Crewreview is free. It uses the coding agents you already have, so their plans and limits apply; the dashboard shows tokens and cost where the harness reports them.
faq.a2: Only to the harness you choose, which is where it already goes when you code with it. Crewreview has no server and no telemetry.
faq.a3: GitHub and GitLab, cloud and self-managed. Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea are next.
faq.q4: Will it post things I didn't approve?
faq.a4: Not unless you switch a repository to auto. New repositories start in inbox mode, and sensitive changes always wait for you.
faq.a5: So it stays open: anyone who ships a modified version, or runs one as a service for others, must share the source.

start.ai_html: Using an AI assistant? Copy a ready-made prompt and paste it into Claude Code, Codex or any agent: it installs Crewreview, checks your setup and links your repositories.
start.aiPrompt:
Set up Crewreview for me. It's a free, open source crew of AI agents that reviews pull requests and answers the reviews on mine: https://github.com/Quost/crewreview. Its guide for agents: https://crewreview.web.app/llms.txt

1. Install the command line tool:
   - macOS or Linux: curl -fsSL https://crewreview.web.app/install.sh | sh (with Homebrew: brew install Quost/crewreview/crewreview)
   - Windows, in PowerShell: irm https://crewreview.web.app/install.ps1 | iex
2. Run crewreview doctor. It needs git, at least one coding agent signed in (Claude Code, Codex or Kiro) and gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab) signed in. If something is missing, tell me how to fix it and wait for me.
3. Ask me which repositories Crewreview should watch. Link each one in inbox mode, so nothing is posted without my approval: crewreview repo add <repository URL> --attend inbox
4. Keep it running and open the dashboard: crewreview service install, then crewreview ui
5. Add Crewreview to the coding agents I use: crewreview mcp setup shows how for each one. In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add Quost/crewreview, then /plugin install crewreview@crewreview

Explain each command before you run it. Never switch a repository to auto mode unless I ask.
